Open a network in MiRA with MiRA's defaults

Source: R/plot_mira.R
plot_mira.Rd

Converts an EMLN multilayer object to JSON and opens MiRA, the Multilayer Interactive Rendering Application, in the default web browser, with MiRA's default view, in the view given by mode. To describe how the plot should look in code, use mira() instead.

Usage

plot_mira(
  multilayer,
  bipartite = FALSE,
  setA_type = NULL,
  directed = NULL,
  directed_interlayer = NULL,
  mode = "network",
  port = 8080,
  mira_path = NULL,
  browser = getOption("browser"),
  viewer = getOption("ggmira.viewer", FALSE)
)

plot_multilayer(
  multilayer,
  bipartite = FALSE,
  setA_type = NULL,
  directed = NULL,
  directed_interlayer = NULL,
  port = 8080,
  mira_path = NULL,
  browser = getOption("browser"),
  viewer = getOption("ggmira.viewer", FALSE)
)

Arguments

multilayer

A multilayer object (created by create_multilayer_network or load_emln).

bipartite

Logical. Whether the network is bipartite. Defaults to FALSE. Bipartite is not auto-detected. When TRUE, the nodes table must contain a node_type column (or node_group, or type, as in the networks of load_emln) with exactly two distinct values across the network. MiRA knows the column as node_type, whatever its name in the data.

setA_type

Optional character. The node_type value to render as Set A (top row) in MiRA's bipartite layout. By ecological convention this is the higher trophic level (e.g. "pollinator", "parasite", "disperser"). Only used when bipartite = TRUE.

directed

Logical or NULL. Whether intralayer links are directed. If NULL (default), auto-detected by checking intralayer edge symmetry.

directed_interlayer

Logical or NULL. Whether interlayer links are directed. If NULL (default), inherits from directed. Interlayer links are directed whenever intralayer links are, so FALSE has no effect on a directed network.

mode

The view MiRA opens in: "network" (default), "grid", "map" (needs latitude and longitude in net$layers), "layer", "meta" (the meta-network), "dashboard" or "data"; each with MiRA's default settings. One view per call: to see a network in two views, call plot_mira() twice. To set a view's options (grid columns, meta-network settings), use mira() with mira_mode_grid() or mira_mode_meta().

port

Integer. Port for the local HTTP server. Default is 8080.

mira_path

Character. Path to the MiRA web-app directory. If NULL (default), uses the copy bundled with the package (system.file("MiRA", package = "ggmira")).

browser

Choose the specific browser to open MiRA in. Defaults to the system default via getOption("browser"). A command that opens a page, as for browseURL: a browser's name where that is a command (e.g. "firefox" on Linux), or on macOS "open -a Firefox". "chrome" works on macOS too. When R is not interactive (a script), a plot opens only when browser is given.

viewer

TRUE to open MiRA in RStudio's Viewer pane instead of the browser (outside RStudio, the browser opens). Defaults to FALSE, or to getOption("ggmira.viewer"): put options(ggmira.viewer = TRUE) in your .Rprofile to always use the pane (the option must be TRUE or FALSE; anything else is an error). A browser given in the call wins. MiRA needs room (at least 1024 x 600 pixels): maximize the pane, or click its Show in new window button to move the plot to the browser.

Value

Invisibly returns the server handle. Use httpuv::stopServer(handle) to stop the server when done. NULL when nothing was opened: R is not interactive (a script, R Markdown) and browser was not given.

Details

The plot is the one MiRA shows for the same network loaded on its website, with two differences: the legends start minimized (as for every plot from R; mira_legends() opens them), and the map and the layer view are fitted to the layers.

plot_multilayer() is the same function without mode (always network mode), under the name emln uses. While emln has a function of that name too, the package attached last provides it: after library(emln), write ggmira::plot_multilayer(), or use plot_mira().

From MiRA back to R. Change the plot in MiRA, then click MiRA's R button (Copy as R code, next to Save Session): it shows the mira() code that draws the current view, starting from this network and these arguments, to paste into a script. Not for plot_multilayer().

The function:

  1. Converts the multilayer object to MiRA's JSON format (the same output as emln::multilayer_to_json)

  2. Starts a local HTTP server (using httpuv) that serves the MiRA app and the network JSON

  3. Opens the browser with auto-load enabled

The server runs in the background. Call httpuv::stopServer(handle) or close R to stop it. The JSON data is kept in memory and never written to disk. MiRA loads its drawing libraries and map tiles from the web, so the plot needs an internet connection.

plot_multilayer() replaces emln::plot_multilayer(): the same arguments and behavior, plus viewer.

Note

MiRA is a browser-based interactive visualization tool for multilayer networks, available at https://mira.ecomplab.com/.

If you use MiRA in published research, please cite:

Nehoray SM, Bloch Y, Pilosof S (2026). Interactively visualizing biological multilayer networks using MiRA. arXiv:2605.09597 [cs.SI]. doi:10.48550/arXiv.2605.09597

Feedback and bug reports: https://github.com/Ecological-Complexity-Lab/MiRA/issues.

See also

mira() to describe the plot in code; mira_mode for the views; emln::load_emln, emln::multilayer_to_json

Examples

library(emln)
net <- load_emln(17)
#> Creating state node map
#> Creating extended link list with node IDs

# Open with MiRA's defaults
plot_mira(net, bipartite = TRUE, setA_type = "bird")
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.

# In another view: the meta-network, or the layers side by side
plot_mira(net, bipartite = TRUE, setA_type = "bird", mode = "meta")
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.
plot_mira(net, bipartite = TRUE, setA_type = "bird", mode = "grid")
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.

# Directed links, on another port
plot_mira(net, bipartite = TRUE, setA_type = "bird",
          directed = TRUE, directed_interlayer = TRUE, port = 9000)
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.

# Another browser; a local copy of MiRA, not the bundled one
# plot_mira(net, browser = "chrome", mira_path = "~/MiRA")

# In RStudio's Viewer pane
# plot_mira(net, bipartite = TRUE, setA_type = "bird", viewer = TRUE)

# The same as plot_mira(net, bipartite = TRUE, setA_type = "bird").
# ggmira:: because emln, attached above, has a plot_multilayer() too
ggmira::plot_multilayer(net, bipartite = TRUE, setA_type = "bird")
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.

# When done, stop the servers
httpuv::stopAllServers()
